children: Chicago grains futures edged higher on Monday morning, as weakness in the US dollar raised hopes for improved export demand for American crops.
Wheat futures were supported by concerns over supplies from the Black Sea region, while soybean gained on meal demand.
The most-traded soybean contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT)
was up 0.51% at $12.27 a bushel at 0147 GMT. CBOT wheat
added 0.25% at $5.93-1/2 a bushel and CBOT corn

The dollar eased off its highest level in more than a year and a half at the start of Asian trade on Monday, as investor confidence recovered after a selloff last week and traders pared bets that the Federal Reserve would hike interest rates aggressively at its meeting next month.
A softer dollar makes US commodities more attractive to importers in the global market.

Grain traders continue to monitor escalating hostilities in the Black Sea export region. At least four people were killed in Russian drone attacks in Ukraine's Kyiv region on Sunday, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy and local officials said.
Under its daily reporting rules, the US Department of Agriculture confirmed private sales of 100,000 metric tons of US soymeal to Spain.
Deforestation rules going into effect in the European Union in late December could steer soymeal export demand toward US supplies, analysts said.

The US soybean crush in October jumped to the largest for any month on record as an accelerating soy harvest replenished crushing supplies, while soyoil stocks rebounded after hitting lowest in nearly 12 years a month earlier, NOPA data showed

India's wheat acreage is poised for its steepest decline in 26 years as fields parched by the weakest monsoon rains in more than a decade spur farmers to switch to competing crops in search of better returns, industry officials told Reuters.

US stock futures attempted a recovery on Monday, while Asian markets slid and authorities around the region readied support measures after a withering wipeout last week for tech and chip stocks at the centre of the AI boom.
